short: VAE-GAN lip-to-speech with a reference-audio voice: a standard design whose gains are in distribution and sync metrics; no WER is reported, behind its own lineage on evaluation.
position: The paper [@hegde2022lip] changes the training target (M02, frozen ASR-encoder content), the decoder (M06, VAE latent with adversarial critic) and voice control (M08, reference-audio embedding); each is standard. Its in-the-wild claim rests on distribution and sync metrics and a listener test on 15 LRS2 samples (Sec. 4.3), without the word error rate its own lineage reported [@prajwal2020learning] (M12, behind on protocol). On LRS2 it beats the authors' sequence-to-sequence baseline on FDSD and sync (LSE-C 2.507 against 1.991) but not on PESQ and STOI (Table 3); content is unmeasured. In the same group's [later], harder test (10 LRS3 sentences of 10 s or longer), its intelligibility is rated 1.07 of 5 against 3.49 for their successor [@hegde2023towards]. SED is not shown to be independent of the voice loss's identity network (Sec. 3.2.7, 4.1.2), and the test-time voice reference is not stated (Sec. 3.2.4). The claim to be the first to handle ambiguity explicitly (Sec. 1) omits an earlier variational-autoencoder model sharing an author [@yadav2021speech] (Appendix).
